channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [6] Single- and two-mode magnon thermal squeezing
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Gerrit E. W. Bauer, Eiji Saitoh

Authors: Tomosato Hioki, Kaito Tojo, Mehrdad Elyasi, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Condensed matter, involving magnons and quantum effects in a ferrimagnetic insulator.

Tags: #magnons #quantummagnets #spintronics #quantuminformation

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03294-4 Obtaining squeezed states in magnets are a key challenge for future spin-based sensing and information technology. Now thermal squeezing of magnons, where noise drops below thermal levels, is shown in a ferrimagnetic insulator device.

item.title: [6] Electron matter waves with internal torque
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: J. Kuttruff, P. Baum

Authors: Y. Fang, J. Kuttruff, P. Baum

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Methodology paper exploring novel electron probes for materials at atomic scales.

Tags: #methodology #electronmicroscopy #materialsscience

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03308-1 Laser light cannot probe or control rotation at the single-atom level in a material. Now electron matter waves with internal torque show promise for studying and manipulating materials on atomic scales.
